title: Limestone County Historical Commission Advances Cemetery Projects, Honors Reconstruction-Era Legislator - NewsBreak
text:
By William Reagan ,
7 hours ago The Limestone County Historical Commission met Dec. 2 at the county courthouse, where members discussed ongoing preservation projects, upcoming events and recent historical recognitions.
Commission members received a report on the Tehuacana Valley Cemetery following a Nov. 25 site visit. The cemetery, which has seen little maintenance for about two decades, is heavily overgrown, members said. Linda Ferris noted that two members of the Tehuacana Historical Society have expressed interest in helping restore the grounds. The commission plans to assist with cleanup efforts and begin an application to designate the site as a Historic Texas Cemetery through the Texas Historical Commission.
Work also continued on a planned tour of Mexia City Cemetery, a project commissioners have collaborated on for several months. Members reviewed a second draft of a brochure that will feature a map and QR codes linking to biographies of selected individuals buried there. Most of the biographies have been completed and are being uploaded to webpages connected to the QR codes. Additional revisions to the brochure are expected before its next draft. The commission also plans to pursue a Texas Historic Cemetery designation for Mexia City Cemetery.
Commissioners Charles McDaniel and William Reagan reported on the Nov. 12 dedication of a Texas Historical Marker honoring David Medlock Jr., an African American legislator who represented Limestone, Falls and McLennan counties during Reconstruction. The marker was installed under Senate Bill 667, which mandated new markers for 23 African American men who served in the Texas Legislature during that era. Reagan said he has posted photographs of the ceremony on the commission’s website.
The commission agreed to participate in the Mexia Christmas parade scheduled for Dec. 5. Ferris also announced that Preservation Texas volunteers will stay at Louisiana Hall on the Trinity/Westminster campus in Tehuacana and host a cleanup day on Dec. 20 from 7 a.m. to noon.
The commission’s next meeting is set for Jan. 6 at the Limestone County Courthouse.
